Limitations: Dependency inventory covers the 34 pinned NuGet packages in packages.config and corresponding vendored JavaScript assets. dotnet list package --include-transitive --format json failed because Microsoft.WebApplication.targets is unavailable; dependencies beyond this pinned inventory were not verified.
CVE findings identify vulnerable versions, not proof that vulnerable features are exercised. Advisory links and branch-specific patched versions are retained with each finding.
CWE findings are source-based assessments; deployment exploitability was not dynamically tested. FOUND and NOT_FOUND describe the inspected patterns, not a security certification.
CWE-22, CWE-23, and CWE-36 describe related pathname handling in the same upload operation. Findings are counts of checklist matches, not counts of distinct root causes.
Assessment severities follow the supplied checklist; optional does not imply that a finding is safe to ignore.
Application source was not modified. Remediations are recommendations for follow-up work.

[CVE-2018-8269](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mv2r-q4g5-j8q5): Denial of service in ASP.NET Core

Severity: HIGH

Affected pinned packages/assets:
- Microsoft.Data.OData:5.6.4 (nuget; WebApp-Storage-DotNet/packages.config:17)
  Applicable vulnerable range: < 5.8.4; first patched version: 5.8.4.

Recommended fix: upgrade to a supported patched version for the applicable branch listed above and verify compatibility. Where no patched version is listed, the advisory provides no fixed version for that branch; do not assume a same-major upgrade fixes it. Update shipped JavaScript assets as well as package declarations.

Coverage: packages.config inventory fallback after dotnet package enumeration failed on missing Microsoft.WebApplication.targets; unresolved dependencies beyond the pinned inventory are not verified. This is a known-vulnerable-version finding, not proof that the vulnerable feature is exercised.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Initialization
CweFindings.Description: The product does not initialize or incorrectly initializes a resource, which might leave the resource in an unexpected state when it is accessed or used.
CweFindings.Explanation: HomeController.blobContainer is left null at application startup and is initialized only by visiting Index. UploadAsync dereferences this shared resource at line 108 without ensuring Index ran. A direct multipart POST after worker startup/recycle therefore reliably raises NullReferenceException; the catch block publishes the detailed exception and stack trace via Error.cshtml. This is a request-order-dependent initialization defect and information exposure, not a memory-corruption claim. Valid storage setup and a request to Index avoid this particular null state.

CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
CweFindings.Description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.
CweFindings.Explanation: The gallery routes expose DeleteImage and DeleteAll with only HttpPost; there is no controller/action authorization, ownership check, global Authorize filter, or web.config authorization restriction. Any reachable anonymous caller can invoke DeleteAll to delete every block blob using the application storage identity (158-162), or DeleteImage to delete a known blob. This confers destructive storage modification permissions to arbitrary site visitors, not merely the intentionally public read access configured at line 66. Exploitation requires a configured storage account and initialized container; lack of anti-forgery checks also permits cross-site form submission.

CweFindings.Name: Insufficient Logging
CweFindings.Description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.
CweFindings.Explanation: Security-critical blob deletion (DeleteImage at 136 and DeleteAll at 162) is followed only by a redirect. No application audit record contains actor, target, outcome, or deletion count. Failure handlers (140-144, 168-172) send the exception to a view instead of recording it. Repository-wide application C# inspection found no audit/logging provider or logging calls; no storage diagnostic configuration is committed. Anonymous bulk deletion can therefore occur without an application-level security event record. External platform/storage logging may exist but cannot be verified from this repository.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.
CweFindings.Explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync passes attacker-controlled multipart files[i].FileName directly to BlobClient.UploadAsync(string path) at line 109, which reads a server-local file rather than the uploaded InputStream. No path containment or authorization is enforced. After Index initializes the client (65-66), a crafted relative or absolute server pathname can copy any process-readable local file into the blob container. Index creates that container with PublicAccessType.Blob and lists the new blob URI (66, 75-78), enabling remote retrieval when Azure storage is configured and public access is permitted. The source extension is retained (181-182), not a path restriction. API contract: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/azure.storage.blobs.blobclient.uploadasync (string path denotes a local file). Pinned 12.9.1 SDK source verification: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/Azure.Storage.Blobs_12.9.1/sdk/storage/Azure.Storage.Blobs/src/BlobClient.cs; UploadAsync(string path, ...) opens new FileStream(path, FileMode.Open, FileAccess.Read) (SDK source lines 1565-1575).

CweFindings.Name: Relative Path Traversal
CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.
CweFindings.Explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync passes attacker-controlled multipart files[i].FileName directly to BlobClient.UploadAsync(string path) at line 109, which reads a server-local file rather than the uploaded InputStream. No path containment or authorization is enforced. After Index initializes the client (65-66), a crafted relative traversal pathname containing .. can copy any process-readable local file into the blob container. Index creates that container with PublicAccessType.Blob and lists the new blob URI (66, 75-78), enabling remote retrieval when Azure storage is configured and public access is permitted. The source extension is retained (181-182), not a path restriction. API contract: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/azure.storage.blobs.blobclient.uploadasync (string path denotes a local file). Pinned 12.9.1 SDK source verification: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/Azure.Storage.Blobs_12.9.1/sdk/storage/Azure.Storage.Blobs/src/BlobClient.cs; UploadAsync(string path, ...) opens new FileStream(path, FileMode.Open, FileAccess.Read) (SDK source lines 1565-1575).

CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
CweFindings.Description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
CweFindings.Explanation: DisplayFilesToUpload concatenates the selected File.name without HTML encoding (80) into html and assigns it to FilesToUpload.innerHTML (85). A filename containing an HTML element with an event handler is interpreted as active markup in the gallery origin. This is a user-assisted DOM XSS path: an attacker must deliver a specially named local file and persuade the victim to select it in the file picker; it is not a remotely triggerable stored upload finding. The sink executes before submission, independently of the server upload failure.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection')
CweFindings.Description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before it is used as an identifier for a resource that may be outside the intended sphere of control.
CweFindings.Explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync uses a multipart filename supplied by the requester as the server-local resource identifier passed to BlobClient.UploadAsync(string path), without restriction to uploaded data or a permitted directory. Once Index initializes the container, this permits selection of any process-readable local file for transfer to Azure blobs. The filename is a local file path, not an upload stream; this is the same root cause as the path-traversal findings.
